questions.prompt: What is the central shift that defines AI engineering versus traditional ML engineering?
choices: Adapting an existing foundation model instead of training one from scratch
questions.rationale: AI engineering starts from a capable foundation model and focuses on adaptation, evaluation, and integration rather than training from scratch.

questions.prompt: Which does the study companion call the hardest and most central skill of AI engineering?
questions.rationale: Open-ended outputs are hard to measure, so evaluation is framed as the central challenge, with evaluation-driven development as the answer.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, when should you finetune a model rather than prompt or use RAG?
questions.model_answer: When prompting and retrieval have run out of room and you need behavior the model won't reliably follow from instructions or context alone — after weighing the data and cost.
questions.rationale: Finetuning adapts the weights and is the right tool once cheaper adaptation levers are exhausted, provided the gain justifies the cost.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between RAG and an agent?
choices: RAG trains the model; agents evaluate it
RAG grounds the model in retrieved context; agents let it plan and call tools across steps
They are two names for the same thing
RAG is only for images; agents are only for text
questions.rationale: RAG supplies the right context via retrieval; agents add the ability to act over multiple steps using tools — each with its own failure modes.

questions.prompt: According to the companion, what most often differentiates one AI application's quality from another's?
questions.rationale: Dataset engineering — curation, quality, deduplication, and synthesis — is presented as the real differentiator, often more than model choice.
